doc.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Where jazz will go next
summary: He thinks jazz is ripe for a major innovator like Coltrane.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: What do you envision — I had said before I felt jazz seems to move so fast. Is it possible to measure where it will be ten years from now?

I don’t really think so. Because you know we’re about ripe for some incredible major innovator to come along, somebody of the status of a Coltrane. They don’t come along that often. I think we’re ripe for someone to come and just blow the lid off this stuff, and open up a whole new direction that we’re not even imagining. I think that’s going to be quite exciting when that happens.
